title: Rethinking Sign Language Translation: The Impact of Signer Dependence on Model Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2609.07965v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Sign Language Translation has advanced with deep learning, yet evaluations remain largely signer-dependent, with overlapping signers across train/dev/test. This raises concerns about whether models truly generalise or instead rely on signer-specific regularities. We conduct signer-fold cross-validation on GFSLT-VLP, GASLT, and SignCL, three leading, publicly available, gloss-free SLT models, on CSL-Daily and PHOENIX14T. Under signer-independent evaluation, performance drops sharply: on PHOENIX14T, GFSLT-VLP falls from BLEU-4 21.44 to 3.59 and ROUGE-L 42.49 to 11.89; GASLT from 15.74 to 8.26; and SignCL from 22.74 to 3.66. We also observe that in CSL-Daily many target sentences are performed by multiple signers, so common splits can place identical sentences in both training and test, inflating absolute scores by rewarding recall of recurring sentences rather than genuine generalisation. translated_title: 重新思考手语翻译：手语者依赖性对模型评估的影响
translated_abstract: 手语翻译随着深度学习的发展而不断进步，但目前的评估方式在很大程度上仍依赖于手语者，即训练/开发/测试集中存在手语者重叠的问题。这引发了人们的担忧：模型究竟是真正具备泛化能力，还是仅仅依赖特定手语者的规律。我们在三个领先的、公开可用的无注释手语翻译模型（GFSLT-VLP、GASLT和SignCL）上，针对CSL-Daily和PHOENIX14T两个数据集进行了手语者折交叉验证。在手语者独立的评估设置下，模型性能急剧下降：在PHOENIX14T上，GFSLT-VLP的BLEU-4从21.44降至3.59，ROUGE-L从42.49降至11.89；GASLT从15.74降至8.26；SignCL从22.74降至3.66。我们还观察到，在CSL-Daily中，许多目标句子由多个手语者执行，因此常见的数据划分方式可能将相同的句子同时置于训练集和测试集中，通过奖励模型对重复句子的记忆而非真正的泛化能力来虚高绝对分数。这些发现表明，依赖手语者的评估方式……
tldr: 该研究通过手语者折交叉验证揭示了当前主流手语翻译模型的评估缺陷：在依赖手语者的评估设置下模型性能被严重高估，切换到手语者独立评估后性能大幅下降，且数据集划分中的句子重复问题进一步虚高了评分。
en_tdlr: This study reveals through signer-fold cross-validation that current sign language translation models are severely overestimated under signer-dependent evaluation, with sharp performance drops under signer-independent settings, and sentence duplication across train/test splits further inflates scores.
